stem: Under RA 9275, the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004, what must a factory get from the DENR before it may discharge wastewater (regulated effluents) into a river?
hints: The name of the document says exactly what it allows the factory to do.
Section 14 of RA 9275 is about the permit to let wastewater out.
Section 14 calls it "the legal authorization granted by the Department to discharge wastewater." Pick the choice whose name matches.

solution.methodName: Find the provision, then match its key words

steps.action: Recall Section 14 of RA 9275: the DENR "shall require owners or operators of facilities that discharge regulated effluents pursuant to this Act to secure a permit to discharge."
steps.why: Effluent is wastewater or other discharge from a known source, such as a factory, that is passed into water or onto land (Section 4(m)).

steps.action: Note what the permit sets: "the quantity and quality of effluent" the facility may discharge into a particular water body.
Note that discharging regulated water pollutants without a valid discharge permit is a prohibited act under Section 27(i).
The answer is a discharge permit.

trapNotes.A barangay clearance: A barangay clearance is a local document. RA 9275 requires a discharge permit from the DENR.
trapNotes.A Certificate of Conformity: This comes from the Clean Air Act (RA 8749, Section 5(e)). It shows that a new vehicle meets the law's requirements.
trapNotes.A building permit: A building permit is about construction. It does not allow anyone to discharge wastewater into a river.

sourceRef.citation: RA 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004), Section 14; see also Sections 4(m) and 27(i)
